payload.name: Extract explicit subjective evaluations
payload.description: Use during candidate extraction when a speaker explicitly describes how an activity, experience, or thing makes them feel using an evaluative adjective (e.g., amazing, thrilling, wonderful).
content: If a speaker uses an explicit evaluative adjective to describe the emotional quality of an activity, experience, or thing, extract a memory candidate recording that description as a preference or state, attributed to the speaker.
Do not require an explicit 'I like' or 'I feel' phrase; the descriptive adjective alone is sufficient.
Do not apply to weak filler adjectives (e.g., 'good', 'nice') in passing pleasantries unless the description is substantive and specific.

solves: During ingestion, the model missed an explicit subjective evaluation (e.g., 'it's amazing') because no rule forced treating evaluative adjectives as memory-worthy. This rule applies to any speaker's emotional characterization of an activity/entity; it excludes objective facts and filler pleasantries.
